lines: Scratches, scuffs, and one strap I do not trust anymore. Nothing I cannot mend.
Wore half the sole off one boot getting back. Worth it.
My boots earned every mark on the road home.
I will be stitching straps until sunrise, but I am here to stitch them.
The night pulled hard. Good seams held.
I came home with scratches, not silence. I prefer scratches.
One sole nearly split and my courage nearly followed.
I can mend the gear. The shaking may take longer.
A buckle caught a blade that would have found my ribs.
I lost my pack when we ran, but I kept the water skin.
The first blow knocked me down before I understood the fight had started.
Someone hauled me behind cover by the back of my armor.
I wrapped my hand with spare leather and kept moving.
The road home felt twice as long after the noise stopped.
I used every useful thing I had packed except the food.
One glove is gone and the hand beneath it is still here.
I did not feel the cut in my shoulder until we were safe.
The gear smells of smoke, sweat, and wet earth.
Practice kept my hands moving when fear emptied my head.
I survived. Let me sit before we discuss doing it again.
